## Solution

The ODE is $(x+2)(x-1)f'(x)=1$, i.e.
$$f'(x)=\frac{1}{(x+2)(x-1)}=\frac{1}{3}\!\left(\frac{1}{x-1}-\frac{1}{x+2}\right).$$

Integrating on each of the three intervals separated by the singularities $x=-2$ and $x=1$:
$$f(x)=\frac{1}{3}\ln\left|\frac{x-1}{x+2}\right|+C_i,\qquad i\in\{1,2,3\},$$
where $C_1$ is the constant on $(-\infty,-2)$, $C_2$ on $(-2,1)$, $C_3$ on $(1,\infty)$.

Set $g(x)=\frac13\ln\left|\frac{x-1}{x+2}\right|$, so $f(x)=g(x)+C_i$ on interval $I_i$.

**Using $f(0)=\tfrac13$** (note $0\in I_2$):
$$g(0)=\tfrac13\ln\!\left|\tfrac{-1}{2}\right|=-\tfrac13\ln 2 \;\Longrightarrow\; C_2=\tfrac13+\tfrac13\ln 2.$$

**Using $f(-3)=f(3)$** (note $-3\in I_1$, $3\in I_3$):
$$g(-3)=\tfrac13\ln\!\left|\tfrac{-4}{-1}\right|=\tfrac13\ln 4,\qquad g(3)=\tfrac13\ln\!\left|\tfrac{2}{5}\right|=\tfrac13\ln\tfrac25.$$
$$C_1-C_3=g(3)-g(-3)=\tfrac13\ln\tfrac25-\tfrac13\ln 4=\tfrac13\ln\tfrac{1}{10}=-\tfrac13\ln 10.$$

**Computing the target** $f(-4)+f(-1)-f(4)$:
- $-4\in I_1$: $g(-4)=\tfrac13\ln\!\left|\tfrac{-5}{-2}\right|=\tfrac13\ln\tfrac52$.
- $-1\in I_2$: $g(-1)=\tfrac13\ln\!\left|\tfrac{-2}{1}\right|=\tfrac13\ln 2$.
- $4\in I_3$: $g(4)=\tfrac13\ln\!\left|\tfrac{3}{6}\right|=-\tfrac13\ln 2$.

Therefore
$$f(-4)+f(-1)-f(4)=\bigl[g(-4)+g(-1)-g(4)\bigr]+(C_1-C_3)+C_2.$$

The bracketed term:
$$g(-4)+g(-1)-g(4)=\tfrac13\ln\tfrac52+\tfrac13\ln 2+\tfrac13\ln 2=\tfrac13\ln\!\left(\tfrac52\cdot 4\right)=\tfrac13\ln 10.$$

Hence
$$f(-4)+f(-1)-f(4)=\tfrac13\ln 10-\tfrac13\ln 10+\tfrac13+\tfrac13\ln 2=\frac{1+\ln 2}{3}.$$

$$\boxed{f(-4)+f(-1)-f(4)=\dfrac{1+\ln 2}{3}}$$
